reviews.comment: The graduate fluids course is tough, and Dr. Borazjani's deep familiarity with the material makes him overlook varying student levels. He mostly reads slides, and exams are harder than assignments. However, he's a lenient grader, valuing approach over the final answer, bonus problems help. Strong multivariable and vector calculus is essential!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take his class. He assumes you already know what he is supposed to be teaching you. Doesn't take student's needs into consideration at all. His homework feedback is utterly useless. Self-study is useless since his exam/homework problems are poorly written so you don't even know what he is asking you to solve.

Dr. Borazjani was pretty good in my opinion. The homework was definitely hard, especially at the beginning of the semester, but it got easier as the course went on. The project isn't too bad, several help videos were posted that walked you through the process. I personally found his lecture slides helpful, but having the book is a good resource.

Dr. Borazjani is probably one of the worst professors I have taken thus far in college. It seems as though he is actively trying to fail his students, and a homework average of 50% is not an uncommon occurrence. This is one of those classes where you have to teach yourself, because his lectures are no help whatsoever.

Do not take this prof! He does not teach the material, HWs take up the whole week to complete, his tests are so abstract not many people pass. And that is another point, there are much more failures in his class than any other prof.
Difficult. Need to go thru the textbook yourself.
